_about: Latitude & Longitude globe (map id latitude-longitude). Written by the editor (Claude) on 2026-09-27 from গ্লোব_অক্ষ_দ্রাঘিমা_খসড়া_৩.xlsx. User decisions 2026-09-27: card values are the conventional (textbook) values; the user will update information later, wherever and however, and it is applied as given. Lines are drawn at the card's values. Imagery: NASA Blue Marble Next Generation, July (credit "NASA Earth Observatory"). Pending: the date line's geometry (Natural Earth file not yet pinned).

factBn.title: Prime meridian (Greenwich)
factBn.states: The Greenwich meridian is a prime meridian, a geographical reference line that passes through the Royal Observatory, Greenwich, in London, England.

timeBn.title: Greenwich Mean Time
timeBn.states: Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) is the local mean time at the Royal Observatory in Greenwich, London, counted from midnight. … The term "GMT" is also used as one of the names for the time zone UTC+00:00

prime-meridian.review: The modern IERS Reference Meridian differs slightly; not shown. Bengali name proposed by the editor; the user may change it. Also called গ্রিনিচ মধ্যরেখা.

factBn.title: Bangladesh Standard Time
factBn.states: The official time signal of BST is determined based on the 90.00° E longitude. This meridian passes through the Harukandi Union, located in the Harirampur Upazila of the Manikganj District, within the Dhaka Division.

factBn.title: International Date Line
factBn.states: It passes through the Pacific Ocean, roughly following the 180.0° line of longitude and deviating to pass around some territories and island groups. Crossing the date line eastbound decreases the date by one day, while crossing the date line westbound increases the date.

date-line.review: geometry is null (pending): it comes from the Natural Earth geographic-lines file once downloaded and pinned; pick the current date line by an exact field value (the file also holds an old pre-1995 segment). Bengali name proposed by the editor; the user may change it.

graticule.review: Generated; 15° as in the mockup. Vertices every 30° or 10° — never 1°/5°/15° — because of the geojson-vt clip-edge bug found in the investigation.

With the conventional 88°01′–92°41′E it would read 87°19′W–91°59′W — the same to the minute. The whole area is ocean (no Natural Earth land inside it). The card shows Bangladesh and its antipode side by side.
